label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Tolu, I'm in Biology 100L right now and I wanted Medicine too. Last year I was exactly where you are, so I'll tell you what it's really like.

First, I'm sorry you've been crying. The day I saw Biology on the portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't even eat. Then my mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months after, and I had to beg her to stop. So whatever you're feeling right now, it's normal. It's not small.

About me: I scored 251 in JAMB 2025, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and got offered Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. 268 is higher than mine, so you're in a stronger position than I was. But let me be honest about the transfer thing, because the two people above both said something that isn't fully true.

Transfer is real. Kingsley, with respect, it's not a myth. People do move. But it is NOT easy, and favour, "just read hard" is too simple. Here's what our level adviser told us:

- You need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L.
- There must be space in Medicine. Even if your grades are perfect, if there's no space, there's no space.
- Last year about 6 people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 applied.

She also said they look at the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME, not only your 100L result. I don't know your school's cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, and you will have to check both. 268 alone doesn't establish that you're eligible. A high score is good, but it doesn't settle anything yet.

As for me, my CGPA after first semester is 4.31. That's not 4.5, so I'm still trying and I can't tell you I've made it. I'm not saying this to scare you. I just don't want anybody accepting Biology thinking the transfer is automatic, because it isn't.

Also, the courses are not a joke. In 100L we're doing BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people. If you're going to chase that 4.5, you have to take those two seriously from day one, not just the Biology courses you'll enjoy. And there are costs too. My lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual was extra. Small small money, but it adds up, so ask your parents to prepare for it.

Now to your real question: is Biology bad? No. It really isn't. I was shocked by this myself. In our first BIO practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and I was fine. Somewhere in that lab I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology way more than I expected. If you had told me last year that I'd be saying this, I would have laughed at you.

Maybe you will feel differently, and that's fine. But I can tell you the course itself is not punishment.

On staying home: favour is right that it's not as easy as people say. I have a classmate from secondary school, Ifeoma. She rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she's still at home. I'm not telling you this so you'll be afraid, because her story is not yours. I'm telling you because the "one year is nothing" line doesn't always hold. Sometimes it's one year, sometimes it turns into three.

But rewriting is also not wrong. If you are really ready, meaning you'll sit down, study, and you can handle the waiting and watching your mates go to school, then it's a valid choice. Some people do it and it works. It just shouldn't be something you do only because your aunty is afraid you'll "finish in Biology", or only because you're hurt right now.

So here's what I would do in your shoes.

1. Go to the faculty or department (or the admissions office) and ask them the exact transfer rules for your own school. Ask what CGPA they need, what JAMB and post-UTME scores they need, how many people were moved last year, and how many applied. Don't just trust forum people, and that includes me. Every school runs it differently and I only know mine.

2. Use the two weeks you have before the acceptance fee deadline. Don't decide from the crying place. Decide after you have the real information.

3. Ask yourself honestly: do you want Medicine, or do you want to be "doctor" for your parents? Your dad is saying accept and your aunty is saying rewrite, and both of them have good intentions, but neither of them will be the one sitting in that lecture hall or that lab. If you really want to treat patients and do that work for years, then that tells you how hard to fight for it. If it's more about what people will say, then maybe give yourself room to think again.

My own choice was to accept, give 100L everything I had, and see. But I'm not you, and I won't tell you what to do. Whatever you pick, accept and try to transfer, accept and settle into Biology, or reject and rewrite, it is not the end of the world. You scored 268. You got admission. You're not a failure. Plenty of people are doing well in places they didn't plan to be.

Also, be a bit gentle with yourself. You've been crying since afternoon, so take a day, eat something, and sleep. Then go and ask those questions at the faculty.

If you want to know anything else about what 100L looks like, I'm here. Just ask. You'll be okay.
